Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:10:1.english: From clearing stones - To remove stones from the vineyard.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:11:1.english: Sealing cracks - That one seals cracks in a tree.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:11:2.english: Is permitted - Because it involves [preventing] a loss.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:11:3.hebrew: אברויי אילני אסור - דהוי משום רווחא. והאי דשרי קשקוש — היינו סתומי פילי, והאי דאסיר — היינו אברויי אילני:
Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:11:3.english: Strengthening trees is prohibited - For it is on account of [extra] benefit. And that [case where] hoeing is permitted — that is [for] sealing cracks; and that [case where] it is prohibited — that is [for] strengthening trees.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:12:1.hebrew: כל מקום שנאמר כלל בעשה ופרט בלא תעשה - כגון הכא, דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ה:ד׳): "ובשנה השביעית שבת שבתון יהיה לארץ" — כלל, היינו עשה; "שדך לא תזרע וכרמך לא תזמור" — פרט, היינו לא תעשה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:12:1.english: Wherever a generalization is stated as a positive [commandment] and a detail as a negative [commandment] - For example, here, as it is written (Leviticus 25:4): “And in the seventh year shall be a Sabbath of solemn rest for the land” — [this is a] generalization, that is, a positive commandment; “you shall not sow your field, nor prune your vineyard” — [this is a] detail, that is, a negative commandment.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:12:2.hebrew: אין דנין אותו בכלל ופרט וכלל - ואף על גב דכתיב כלל בתריה, כגון הכא דכתיב בתריה (שבת) שבתון — כלומר: אין לו דין דשאר כלל ופרט וכלל שכתובין כולו בעשה או בלאו, דאמר: ״כלל ופרט וכלל, אי אתה דן אלא כעין הפרט״, דמרבי כל מידי דדמי לפרט; אלא דיינינן ליה בכלל ופרט. הואיל דנשתנה משאר כלל ופרט וכלל, אמרינן: ״אין בכלל אלא מה שבפרט״ — הני אין, מידי אחרינא לא:
Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:12:2.english: One does not apply to it [the rule of] a generalization, and a detail, and a generalization - Even though a generalization is written after it — such as here, where “(a Sabbath of) complete rest” is written after it — that is to say, it does not have the law of other [cases of] a generalization, a detail, and a generalization, which are written entirely as a positive [commandment] or as a negative [commandment], where one says: “A generalization, a detail, and a generalization — you judge only according to what is similar to the detail,” which includes anything that is similar to the detail. Rather, we judge it as a generalization and a detail. Since it differs from other [cases of] a generalization, a detail, and a generalization, we say: “There is nothing in the generalization other than what is in the detail” — these, yes; anything else, no.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:15:1.english: Everyone does not hold [in accordance with the principle] of Ravin, etc.; the one who said he is flogged, [all is] well - As [the Gemara] said, that we expound [the verses] by [the principle of] a generalization, a detail, and a generalization.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:16:1.english: [For] another [subcategory], not - That is why [one who] plows is not flogged.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:1:1.hebrew: תולדות - כגון משקה זרעים, שלא היה במשכן, לא אסר רחמנא:
Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:1:1.english: Subcategories - Such as watering seeds, which was not [performed] in the Tabernacle, the Merciful One did not prohibit [them].

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:2:1.english: Pruning is included in sowing - For the way of one who prunes is to make fruit grow, like one who sows.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:2:2.hebrew: בצירה - בענבים כקצירה בתבואה, וקצירה אב מלאכה היא בפ' כלל גדול (שבת דף עג.). בצירה בכלל קצירה — דשניהן חותכין:
Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:2:2.english: Harvesting grapes - [Applies] to grapes as reaping [applies] to grain; and reaping is a primary category of labor in the chapter [entitled] Klal Gadol (Shabbat 73a). Harvesting grapes is included in reaping, as both involve cutting.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:4:1.english: Pruning - Cutting dried branches of a grapevine.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:4:2.english: Hoeing - That one digs beneath the vines to loosen the soil.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:4:3.hebrew: כיסוח - בעשבים, שחותך הרעים מן הטובים. ולא היינו ניכוש — דמעקר העיקרים מן הקרקע, דלזה אין עוקרין, אלא חותכין למעלה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:4:3.english: Trimming - [Applies] to herbs, where one cuts the bad from the good. And this is not [the same as] weeding, as [in that case] one uproots the roots from the ground, whereas for this, one does not uproot [them], but rather cuts [them] above [the ground].

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:4:4.hebrew: תלמוד לומר שדך לא כרמך לא - מדלא כתיב ״לא תזרע שדך, לא תזמור כרמך״, אלא ״שדך לא תזרע, כרמך לא תזמור״ — משמע: ״שדך לא, כרמך לא״:
Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:4:4.english: The verse states: “Your field [you shall] not; your vineyard [you shall] not” - Since it is not written: “You shall not sow your field; you shall not prune your vineyard,” but rather: “Your field you shall not sow; your vineyard you shall not prune,” it implies: “Your field [you shall] not; your vineyard [you shall] not.”

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:5:1.hebrew: מקרסמין - היינו זימור, אלא שקירסום שייך באילנות:
Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:5:1.english: Pruning - This is [the same as] pruning [vines, zimur], except that [the term] kirsum applies to trees.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:5:2.hebrew: מזרדין - מחתך ענפים יבשים ולחים, לפי שיש לאילן ענפים יותר מדאי:
Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:5:2.english: Trimming branches - Cutting dry and fresh branches, because the tree has too many branches.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:5:3.english: Mefasegin - Supporting the tree that is excessively lush.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:6:1.english: They fertilize - They place manure at the base of the tree.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:6:2.english: One removes [stones] - [Removing] stones that are upon the base of the tree.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:6:3.hebrew: מאבקים - ששרשיו נראין, ומכסין אותו באבק:
Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:6:3.english: Covering with dust - Where its roots are exposed, and they cover it with dust.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:6:4.hebrew: מעשנין - עושין עשן תחת האילן, כדי שינשרו התולעים שעליו:
Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:6:4.english: Fumigate - One makes smoke under the tree so that the worms on it will fall off.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:7:1.hebrew: יקשקש - היינו עידור, אלא שעידור בגפנים וקשקוש בזיתים:
Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:7:1.english: [One may] hoe lightly - That is [the same as] hoeing, except that hoeing is [the term used] for grapevines, and hoeing lightly for olive trees.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:7:2.english: Circular ditches - Digging a pit under the grapevine to put water into it.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:7:3.hebrew: לא יקשקש תחת הזיתים ולא יעדר כו' - ואם תקשי: הא אסר עידור לעיל? — קא תריץ לקמן בעוגיות: הא בחדתי והא בעתיקי, והוא הדין לעידור:
Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:7:3.english: One may not hoe lightly under olive trees and one may not hoe, etc. - And if you should object: But didn't it forbid hoeing above? — [the Gemara] resolves [it] below with regard to circular ditches: This is with new ones, and that is with old ones; and the same applies to hoeing.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:8:1.english: Sowing was included in the general rule - [As it is written:] “And in the seventh year shall be a sabbath of solemn rest, etc.”

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:8:2.hebrew: אף כל עבודה שהיא בשדה ובכרם - כגון כל הני פרטי. יצא קשקוש, ועידור, ומים בנקעים, ועוגיות, שאינן בשניהן, כו':
Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:8:2.english: So too, any labor that is in the field and in the vineyard - Such as all these specific labors [prohibited above]. Excluded are light hoeing, and hoeing, and [filling] fissures with water, and [making] circular ditches, which are not [performed] in both of them, etc.

Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:9:1.hebrew: כל הני מדרבנן - אבל מדאורייתא לא הוי אלא זמירה ובצירה, כדאמרינן לעיל: הני אין, מידי אחרינא לא:
Rashi on Moed Katan 3a:9:1.english: All these are rabbinic - But by Torah law, there are only pruning and grape picking, as we said above: These, yes; anything else, no.

Tosafot on Moed Katan 3a:12:1.hebrew: אין דנין אותו בכלל ופרט וכלל - הכי הוה שמיע ליה לר' אילעא, דכיון דהפרט בלא תעשה, הכלל האחרון אינו מוציא הפרט ממשמעותיה, ואינו כלל ופרט וכלל, דדיינינן ליה בכלל ופרט. ולא נהירא לי: דמנלן דרבי אילעא ס"ל הכי? אימא דהפרט שהוא בלא תעשה בטל, אבל הכלל עומד במקומו לפי דבריו! ועוד, לפי לשון זה קשה לי: אמאי תירץ דכולי עלמא לית להו דר' אבין? והא הוה מצי לתרוצי דכולי עלמא אית להו, דבכל מקום סוגיית הש"ס היא, דכיון דמצי למימר דכולי עלמא אית להו סברת האמורא — לא מתרצינן לית להו! ולימא הכי: דכולי עלמא אית להו דרבי אבין; מאן דאמר אינו לוקה — שפיר, ומאן דאמר לוקה — סבירא ליה כי הך ברייתא דמפקא ליה לתולדות מקרא, וקסבר: לאו אסמכתא הוא, אלא דרשה גמורה היא. ולי נראה: דהא "לימא בדר' אבין אמר ר' אילעא וכו'" קאזיל בכה"ג דליכא הכא אלא כלל ופרט, דכלל בתרא לא חשיב, כיון דהאי כלל בקרא אחרינא, וחשיב בכלל המרוחק זה מזה כיון דלא הוו בחד קרא — דהכי מוכח בפ"ק דפסחים (דף ו: ושם), דאיכא למאן דאמר: כיון דהוו בתרי קראי לא מיצטרפי למיהוי כלל ופרט וכלל, והכא נמי לא הוי אלא כלל ופרט. והכי איכא הגירסא [בירושלמי דכלאים] בפ"ח: "חד אמר לוקה — סבר לה כרבי אילעא, דאינו נדון בכלל ופרט; כיון דהפרט בלא תעשה, הפרט בטל והכלל במקומו עומד, ולפיכך אמר כל החורש בשביעית לוקה. וחד אמר החורש בשביעית אינו לוקה — לא סבר להא דר' אילעא, אלא דנין אותו בכלל ופרט: הני — אין, מידי אחרינא — לא". ודחי לה: דכולהו אית להו דרבי אילעא; מאן דאמר לוקה — שפיר, ומאן דאמר אינו לוקה — מכדי זמירה בכלל זריעה ובצירה כו'. ואם נפשך לומר: למאן דאמר לוקה, אמאי כתב רחמנא זמירה ובצירה? שמא קסבר: ללאו יתירא אתי. אי נמי קסבר: כרם משדה לא הוה יליף, הלכך הוצרך למיכתב בין בשדה בין בכרם:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 3a:12:1.english: "One does not apply [the principle of] a generalization, a detail, and a generalization" - This is what was understood as Rabbi Ile’a’s view: that since the detail is [formulated as] a negative prohibition, the final generalization does not extract the detail from its [restricted] meaning, and it is not [treated as] a generalization, a detail, and a generalization, but rather we judge it as a generalization and a detail [alone]. But this is not clear to me: For from where do we know that Rabbi Ile’a holds this? Say [instead] that the detail, which is [formulated as] a negative prohibition, is nullified, but the generalization stands in its place according to his words! And furthermore, according to this formulation, it is difficult to me: Why did [the Gemara] answer that everyone does not accept [the statement] of Rabbi Avin? But it could have answered that everyone accepts it! For everywhere, the methodology of the Talmud is that since one can say that everyone accepts the Amora's logic, we do not answer that they do not accept it! And let [the Gemara] say this: Everyone accepts [the statement] of Rabbi Avin; the one who says he is not flogged is fine, and the one who says he is flogged holds like that baraita which derives the subcategories from Scripture, and he holds that it is not [merely] an asmakhta [support], but an absolute derivation. And it appears to me: That this [suggestion of the Gemara], "Let us say they disagree regarding [the statement] of Rabbi Avin [who] said [in the name of] Rabbi Ile’a, etc.", proceeds on the assumption that here there is only a generalization and a detail; for the latter generalization is not considered, since this generalization is in a different verse, and it is considered among generalizations distant from one another since they are not in a single verse. For so it is proven in the first chapter of Pesachim (6b and there), that there is one who says that since they are in two verses, they do not combine to become a generalization, a detail, and a generalization; and here too, it is only a generalization and a detail. And so is the textual reading [in the Yerushalmi of Kilayim] in chapter 8: "One said he is flogged, holding like Rabbi Ile’a that it is not judged as a generalization and a detail; since the detail is [formulated as] a negative prohibition, the detail is nullified and the generalization stands in its place, and therefore he said that anyone who plows in the Sabbatical Year is flogged. And one said one who plows in the Sabbatical Year is not flogged, not holding this [view] of Rabbi Ile’a, but rather we judge it as a generalization and a detail: these, yes; anything else, no." And [the Gemara] rejects this: Everyone accepts [the principle of] Rabbi Ile’a; the one who says he is flogged is fine, and the one who says he is not flogged [holds]: After all, pruning is included in sowing, and grape harvesting, etc. And if you wish to say: According to the one who says he is flogged, why did the Merciful One write pruning and grape harvesting? Perhaps he holds: They come for an extra negative prohibition. Alternatively, he holds: [The law of] a vineyard could not have been derived from a field; therefore, it was necessary to write [it] both regarding a field and regarding a vineyard.

Tosafot on Moed Katan 3a:8:1.hebrew: אף כל שבשדה ושבכרם - וכל הני עבודות דלעיל נוהגות בין בשדה ובין בכרם. ואפילו שיש מהן שאין עתה נוהגין כן — י"ל שבמקומן היו עושין כך, ורגילין לעשותן בשדה ובכרם:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 3a:8:1.english: "So too, any [labor] in the field and in the vineyard" - And all these labors [mentioned] above are practiced both in the field and in the vineyard. And even though there are some of them that [people] do not currently practice in this way, it can be said that in their locale they would do so, and were accustomed to perform them in the field and in the vineyard.
